newsitem.title: USA: US Sen Lott hopes for budget announcement soon.
newsitem.headline: US Sen Lott hopes for budget announcement soon.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Wednesday he hopes an announcement can be made on the budget talks early next week, after he confers with President Clinton.

Speaking to reporters, the Mississippi Republican said he planned to talk with the president "not later than next Tuesday." Asked if he then would have a budget announcement, he replied, "We would hope."
"I think that we will have a good feel by the end of the week and we hopefully will have something to announce by the first part of next week," he said.

"You can't keep going on indefinitely, (in budget talks). I do worry that our people are getting hardened on both ends," Lott said. Lengthy talks raise the prospect that each side will lose support for the compromises reached in the final plan, he added.

But Senate Finance Committee chairman Bill Roth, Republican of Delaware, warned party leaders Wednesday the budget agreement with the White House should not give his panel detailed instructions on the tax cuts.
The Finance Committee intends to exert its right to draft tax cut and Medicare spending legislation, Lott said.

For that reason, a final budget agreement with the White House might include general statements on the size of tax cuts and spending cuts without including the type of detail needed to bring specific legislation to a vote.

Senate Republican Whip Don Nickles of Oklahoma said he urged senators at the Republican lunch to remain flexible and not draw limits for the budget. "Allow us a little flexibility to achieve results," he said he told his colleagues.
